subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What native SKILL.md trust model should OpenClaw adopt for third-party skills: advisory verification only, runtime signature enforcement, or staged enforcement tied to capability policy?
rationale: This choice defines the permanent trust root, signature envelope, issuer/revocation semantics, unsigned defaults, and upgrade behavior for third-party instructions loaded into agent context.

options.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
options.body: Define signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory
options.body: Keep ClawHub verify output and install provenance as user-visible trust signals without runtime blocking until maintainers choose stronger enforcement.

options.title: Split design first
options.body: Track issuer format, ClawHub metadata, loader checks, capability policy, and migration as separate owner-reviewed design tasks before implementation.

recommendation.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
recommendation.body: Define signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest visible review signal on this canonical security/product boundary and is already routing the issue as maintainer follow-up.
